in_latin.name: Eduardus
in_latin.meaning: Nomen masculinum ex Germanico et Gothico derivatum, significans fortis et prosperus
in_latin.long_meaning: Eduardus est nomen masculinum, quod a Germanico et Gothico derivatum est. Insignificat fortitudo et prosperitatem. Ex origine, Eduardus erat nomen regum Anglorum, qui a 9o saeculo usque ad 11um saeculum regnaverunt. In historia Christiana, Eduardus fuit nomen sancti, qui in Ecclesia Catholica et Ecclesia Anglicana veneratur.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eduard reached its peak popularity in the 19th and early 20th centuries, particularly in Europe and the United States. It is a name that connotes a sense of wealth, protection, and wisdom. In some cultures, it is also believed that the name Eduard carries a sense of nobility and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Eduard holds a deeper spiritual meaning. It is a reminder of the rich grace and blessings that God bestows upon us, making us His guardians and stewards of His creation. It is also a reminder of St. Edward the Confessor, who stood firm in his faith amid the political upheaval of his time and is remembered as a model of faithfulness and unwavering commitment to God. Therefore, Eduard is a name that inspires us to be rich in grace, firm in our faith, and good stewards of God's blessings.

historical_references.reference: Eduard I, The Confessor, was the Duke of Swabia from 1245 to 1268 and was the founder of the Swabian Anonymous Brotherhood, a charitable organization. He was also a Wittelsbach prince, the second son of Duke Otto I of Swabia and Agnes of Hohenstaufen.

Eduard I, The Black Prince, was the eldest son of King Edward III of England and Queen Philippa of Hainault. He became the Prince of Wales and largely ruled the country during his father's campaigns in France. He was also known as 'The Black Prince' due to his participation in the Battle of Poitiers, where he defeated the French army and captured their king, Jean II.
